Folks — forwarding Skybound counters and the ask from procurement. Quick internal notes / proposed compromise before we take back a final redline: 

1) BYOK scope: offer BYOK for Dedicated and Private only. For Hosted, offer envelope encryption and attestations around key separation but not true CMK control. That aligns with our rollout and keeps Hosted customers on the standard key lifecycle.

2) Key rotation: standard 90-day rotation in Exhibit C, but allow customers to opt into more frequent rotation for CMKs in Dedicated/Private; customers get control over rotation cadence for their own CMKs. Add language on emergency access: Redwood will not escrow customer CMKs; for lawful requests we will provide logs and assist with lawful processes but will not disclose key material without a court order and documented multi-party approvals.

3) Access reviews: agree to quarterly access reviews for personnel with production key access; include requirement for audit log retention (12 months minimum, 24 months for enterprise customers if requested as add-on).

4) Subprocessor objection: accept 30-day notice + 14-day objection window for EU-critical subprocessors; objections considered in good faith and escalated to execs if unresolved.

If legal signs off, I'll produce a cleaned Exhibit C (technical notes attached: ExhibitC_TechnicalNotes_20261108.md) and propose we push to DocuSign for final signatures. Also, procurement wants SOC 2 Type II under NDA — Marissa, can you arrange secure share (Box link) and confirm we can send to purchasing@skyboundtech.com?

Diego

[Attachment: ExhibitC_TechnicalNotes_20261108.md — internal technical breakdown of key flow for CMK import/export restrictions, KMS integration steps, and sample KMS policy templates.]

Amir — thank you and thanks for the productive back-and-forth. Per the compromises outlined below, Redwood is prepared to finalize the attached DPA with the updated Exhibit C. Key points included in the executed DPA:

- BYOK: Available for Dedicated and Private deployments. Exhibit C includes the technical import process, customer responsibilities for key rotation when using CMKs, and a statement that Redwood will not escrow customer key material.
- Key rotation: default 90-day rotation for Redwood-managed keys (Hosted/Dedicated default). Customers using CMKs may select a custom rotation cadence and are responsible for their key lifecycle.
- Access controls & logging: quarterly access reviews, role-based access matrix included in Exhibit C, and audit log retention of 12 months (option to extend to 24 months for enterprise add-on).
- Subprocessors & transfers: 30-day notice for EU-facing subprocessors with 14-day objection window; SCCs reflected as the data transfer mechanism.

DocuSign envelope: https://app.docusign.com/exec?doc=0a1b2c3d4e (executed copy attached). We have also shared the SOC 2 Type II report via secure Box link under NDA; Marissa confirmed the upload to procurement earlier today.
